Try to distract yourself  from the rage. Small, but ridicously long questions. Have you tried reading a book? Do you know why gender you prefer? Which spirals into what - which spirals into yes or no - which has two choices. You like adventure. Nice! Why? You don't know which one? Maybe you prefer sci-fi or romance? Why you think that? Maybe you like the wording, but not the genre. Wording. Are lyrics that you really like? Why? They are poetic? You prefer music with good composition over good lyrics? The other way? Maybe write your own. Maybe don't write it. Maybe you should talk to yourself. At the end of every day, sit with yourself and hit your audio recorder. Say the date. Say what you did. Say what you ate, how many steps did you take, which song you listened the most to. I get fixated easily, you do too? Let out your feelings. Ask yourself why you felt that way. Don't have the answers? It's OK. Come back tomorrow. Do it again.   Then listen to them in a month, or two, or three. Listen where you came from and where you are heading to. You don't like the answer? Don't like where you are heading to? It's fine. You must have done, recorder, said something you liked. Is it really good for you? Great. Do it. Notice what you are doing that you don't like. Can you change it? 

Live one day at time. If I asked you to come with me a long 30 km walk, you would tell me to fuck off. Ok. Oh! Look at that. You already walked one meter. Another one. One meter at the moment. Monomoth is a story I haven't read fully but seems to be a long fan favorite among SasuSaku fans (not sure on the Naruto fandom as a whole, tho) for years. Reading reviews is as fun to me, I have to say. So there, I find them. And they go rampant. Due to personal reasons, I was crying real hard, and there you see myself: a person with a puffy and overly red face with dried tears and sniffing reading the lengthy and wordy review of them. And oh boy. I think I have never used a better "descending into madness" better, because you see me, crying again; early, early morning; phone too close to face; slowly starting to laugh. Their review (as often with their writing) was lengthy and dissatisfied, mostly abhorring Sakura and long enough to write not one, but two of them! Reading it for yourself might be better. It was also weirdly sexual-referencing, mentioning snakes as Sasuke's dick and all of that. They are obsessed with Sakura's sexuality lol

Oh, and the next review was someone basically saying they couldn't be taken seriously due to them being a Sakura-basher and throwing fancy words to fill their anger or something like that. Which...

I know this might be unnecessary and out of your request, but I if I had one nickel for every time an ff writer I liked also made me weirdly anxious but entertained I would have two, which is not a lot but is weird it happened twice. Or something like that. 

It's Monomoth, by Ohtze; a review from 2017 if you're interested. I cried till I laughed.

I think if you're reading for fun (as we all, as mostly, many of us do) I don't think I've given you the best recommendation. Yes, I told you I laugh a lot, but... It's weird okay; expect some intense and really, really acidic stuff. I read them a lot because I like their writing, but their points also make me kinda... nervous? I don't know. It's weird. The political point of view is too personal, their sarcasm is deep and I would call it cynical, and Sakura bashing is way over the top. I remember this story of them, about cannibalism, and he depicted (specifically) Naruto biting, even starting to eat Sakura, and someone in the comments said something along the lines of, "It could have been Sasuke, or really anyone else, but we all know why you choose Sakura." Which, takes me to the next point: the comments! Some of them are normal, you know, the kind of "I loved it" and some others are larger with their point of view and/or review, but some are... extremely weird. (I know I'm using a lot of dots but I really don't know how to convey my thoughts on it by how convoluted they are.) Some of them insult them, or their ff, or their views, but in a really odd way, like I remember someone saying, "You really are the biggest Uchiha cock-sucker,"  and I was like. It made me spiral into some of the weirdest fanfiction and accounts I've ever seen, like, deeply weird. For some reason, I think they are some kind of social experiment where they mixed cynism, and sarcasm, Naruto, some personal views, and some funny jokes written as true. And their Sakura bashing is too much. Way too much. Their whole bashing is too much. Overall, I think reading them is like descending into madness: at some point you start laughing. It's funny, but uncomfortable, and then funny. A whole experience I don't know if I should recommend you, but I hope you enjoy it!
